h1: The 8 Best Robot Pool Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Robot Pool Vacuums 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 robot pool vacuums scored on pool size, waterline coverage and runtime, from AIPER cordless units to Dolphin Nautilus models.
summary: The AIPER Scuba V3 is the best robot pool cleaner for typical in-ground pools: AI vision, no cord and floor-to-waterline coverage. The AIPER Scuba S1 offers 270 minutes for irregular pools, and the Dolphin Nautilus CC Plus handles in-ground pools up to 40 feet. Flat above-ground pools do well with the Y20 or Coasteering.
intro: Pool owners usually shop robot cleaners by brand and discover the mismatch in week one. A cleaner built for a flat 15 foot above-ground pool skips the steps and ledges of a 35 foot in-ground one. A model tuned for wall climbing wastes its battery on a pool that mostly needs floor coverage. Size and bottom shape decide everything, long before a logo does.

So the ranking starts with pool size and bottom type, then adds runtime, waterline ability and whether the cleaner is cordless or corded. We reviewed eight models from AIPER, Dolphin and newer makers, scored them on the Primea framework, and noted which pool each suits. A runtime figure only helps when you compare it with your pool's length or area.

products.name: AIPER Scuba V3 AI Vision Cordless Robotic Pool Cleaner
products.verdict: AI vision mapping, no cord, and floor-to-waterline cleaning. The most capable cordless unit here.
products.description:
The AIPER Scuba V3 is a cordless cleaner with AI vision navigation, floor, wall and waterline coverage and top-load basket access, in the $500+ tier. Vision-based routing plans a path instead of bouncing at random, which cuts the repeat passes that drain a cordless battery before the pool is clean.

It ranks first because it combines routing intelligence with full coverage and no cord. The Scuba S1 runs longer but lacks vision routing, and the Dolphin models are corded.

Buy it for a typical in-ground pool that needs full coverage. The caveat is price, which sits in the premium bracket, and a runtime shorter than the S1's 270 minutes, so skip it for a small above-ground pool where a cheaper cleaner does the job.
cons: Runtime shorter than the Scuba S1
products.idealFor: Typical in-ground pools needing full coverage.
products.skipIf: You have a small above-ground pool and want the cheapest option.

products.name: AIPER Scuba S1 Robotic Pool Cleaner
products.verdict: 270 minutes of runtime, 11 sensors and shallow-area cleaning. Built for irregular pools.
products.description:
The AIPER Scuba S1 lists a 270 minute runtime, 11 sensors with app control, weekly custom scheduling, and cleaning of the floor, walls, waterline and shallow areas. Shallow-area coverage matters for steps and ledges, which many robots skip because they cannot work at that depth.

It ranks second since it has no AI vision routing and costs a premium. Against the V3, the S1 wins on runtime, which is the number that matters most on a big or irregular pool.

Buy it for a large or irregular pool with ledges and steps. Skip it if your pool is small and flat, since you would pay for runtime and sensors you never use. The app scheduling means the pool is clean before the weekend without any effort.
products.idealFor: Large or irregular pools with ledges and steps.
products.skipIf: Your pool is small and flat.

products.name: Dolphin Nautilus CC Plus Robotic Pool Vacuum
products.verdict: Corded, wall-climbing and rated for in-ground pools up to 40 feet. The big-pool workhorse.
products.description:
The Dolphin Nautilus CC Plus is a corded in-ground cleaner rated for pools up to 40 feet, with a wall-climbing scrubber brush and smart navigation. A cord gives unlimited runtime, so size is limited by the cable and the rating rather than a battery. Smart navigation reduces overlapping passes.

It ranks third because the cord can tangle on steps and ladders, and it suits in-ground pools only. It beats the CC Automatic on length rating, 40 feet against 33.

Buy it for a large in-ground pool where a battery would run out. Skip it if you dislike cords or have an above-ground pool. Lay the cable out straight before each run, as twists are what stall a corded robot.
products.idealFor: Large in-ground pools up to 40 feet.
products.skipIf: You dislike cords or have an above-ground pool.

products.name: Dolphin Nautilus CC Automatic Robotic Pool Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: A proven corded cleaner with a scrubber brush for walls. Rated for pools up to 33 feet.
products.description:
The Dolphin Nautilus CC Automatic is a corded cleaner with a wall-climbing scrubber brush, top-load filter access, and a rating up to 33 feet for above-ground or in-ground pools. The scrubber brush matters for algae-prone walls, where a smooth-tracked robot only glides over the film.

It ranks fourth since the 33 foot rating is below the Plus's 40, and the cord needs management. It does fit both pool types, which the Plus does not.

Buy it for an average pool up to 33 feet with walls that grow algae. Skip it if your pool is longer than 33 feet. Top-load access makes emptying quick, but cord management remains the main chore.
pros: Scrubber brush for walls and algae
cons: Lower length rating than the Plus
products.idealFor: Average pools up to 33 feet with algae-prone walls.
products.skipIf: Your pool is longer than 33 feet.

products.name: Cordless Robotic Pool Cleaner, 180-Min Runtime, 3L Basket
products.verdict: 180 minutes, a 3L basket and coverage up to 2200 sq ft. The cordless value choice.
products.description:
The 180 minute cordless cleaner has a 3L debris basket, auto-parking, coverage up to 2200 sq ft and works in above-ground and in-ground pools. A 3L basket handles leaves better than a small fine-debris filter, and 180 minutes covers a medium pool on one charge.

It ranks fifth because it has no smart routing and puts less emphasis on the waterline. The AIPER models route intelligently and clean the tile line. It is the value pick among cordless units.

Buy it for a budget cordless cleaner with a large basket. Skip it if waterline scum is your main concern. Auto-parking brings it to the wall for retrieval, which saves fishing with a pole.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers wanting cordless with a big basket.
products.skipIf: Waterline scum is your main concern.

products.name: EZIOOV U8 Cordless Robotic Pool Cleaner
products.verdict: Built around wall and waterline cleaning with auto-climb and auto-docking.
products.description:
The EZIOOV U8 is a cordless cleaner focused on walls and the waterline, with auto-climb, a 150 minute runtime, auto-docking and coverage up to 2600 sq ft. The waterline is where oils and scum collect, and a robot that climbs and scrubs it saves hand scrubbing.

It ranks sixth because the brand is newer with less track record, and its runtime is shorter than the S1's. It targets walls over the floor, so debris on the bottom gets less attention.

Buy it for an in-ground pool with waterline scum. Skip it if floor debris is your main problem. Auto-docking helps retrieval, but check how well it handles your pool's steps before relying on it.
products.skipIf: Floor debris is your main problem.

products.name: Y20 Robotic Pool Cleaner for Above Ground and Flat Pools
products.verdict: Dual motors and auto-parking for small flat pools up to 1100 sq ft.
products.description:
The Y20 is a cordless cleaner for above-ground and flat in-ground pools, with dual motors, a 120 minute runtime, auto-parking and coverage up to 1100 sq ft. Dual motors give steady traction on a flat floor, and the sizing suits a standard above-ground pool.

It ranks seventh because it is for flat pools only, and 1100 sq ft is its limit. Against the Coasteering, it covers more area and costs a bit more.

Buy it for a standard above-ground pool. Skip it if the pool is large or the bottom slopes. A sloped floor defeats the traction design, so match it to a level bottom.
pros: Dual motors on a flat floor
products.skipIf: Your pool is large or has a sloped bottom.

products.name: Coasteering Planet Edge Pool Vacuum for Above Ground Pool
products.verdict: A compact dual-motor unit for flat above-ground pools up to 850 sq ft.
products.description:
The Coasteering Planet Edge is a cordless dual-motor vacuum for above-ground pools, with a 120 minute runtime, an adjustable cleaning path and coverage for flat pools up to 850 sq ft. It is the lightest and cheapest unit, easy to lift in and out.

It ranks last because 850 sq ft is the smallest coverage limit here and it handles flat pools only. The Y20 covers more for a modest increase.

Buy it for a small flat above-ground pool. Skip it if your pool exceeds 850 square feet. An adjustable path lets you tailor the pattern, but check the weight and basket access before buying.

whatMatters.detail: Cleaners are rated by pool length or square footage. Measure your pool in feet and compare it with the stated limit, which might be 33 feet, 40 feet or 2200 sq ft. A cleaner rated below your size will run out of battery or miss areas, so measure the longest dimension and the area of the floor, including any deep end or shelf.

Cordless units need no cable and are easy to move but run on battery, so check the runtime in minutes against your pool size. Corded units keep running but the cord can tangle on steps and ladders. Read the listing for the minutes figure, such as 180 or 270, and ignore vague battery claims without one, since marketing runtime is a best case.

Many budget cordless units are for flat-bottom pools only. Sloped or deep-end pools need a cleaner that climbs and keeps traction. Look for the words flat pools in the title or specs. The Y20 and Coasteering both list them, so a pool with a sloping floor or a deep end needs a different machine.

The waterline is where oils and scum collect. Cleaners that list waterline cleaning or auto-climb do the tile line, while floor-only models leave it for you to scrub. Check the spec bullets for the word waterline. The AIPER Scuba models and EZIOOV U8 list it, while the 180-minute unit puts less focus there.

A 3 litre basket takes leaves better than a small fine-debris filter. A top-load design lets you empty it without lifting the whole unit out of the water. Look for basket litres and access type in the listing, and note that a full basket cuts suction, so bigger baskets last longer between empties, which matters under trees.

faq.q: How long should a robot pool cleaner run?
faq.a: Match runtime to pool size. A 120 minute unit like the Y20 suits a small flat pool, while the AIPER Scuba S1 at 270 minutes is better for large or irregular pools with steps and ledges to work around.

faq.q: Do robot pool cleaners climb walls?
faq.a: Some do. The Dolphin Nautilus CC models and the EZIOOV U8 list wall climbing or auto-climb. Flat-pool models like the Y20 and Coasteering Planet Edge are for the floor only, so they leave the walls and waterline to you.

faq.q: Is the AIPER Scuba V3 worth more than a budget cordless model?
faq.a: If you want AI vision routing and waterline coverage, yes. For simple floor cleaning on a smaller pool, the budget 180-minute unit does the basics for less, though it lacks smart routing.

faq.q: Can a cordless cleaner run on a large pool?
faq.a: Only if its battery lasts long enough to finish a cycle. Check the runtime against pool size. For pools around 40 feet, a corded Dolphin Nautilus CC Plus avoids battery limits entirely.

faq.q: How often should I empty the basket?
faq.a: After every cycle if you have trees nearby, otherwise weekly. A full basket reduces suction. Top-load designs like the AIPER Scuba V3 make this quick without lifting the unit out of the pool.

faq.q: Do I need to take the cleaner out of the pool?
faq.a: Cordless cleaners with auto-parking, such as the 180-minute unit and Y20, park at the wall for easy retrieval. Always remove the cleaner before shocking the pool or letting it sit for days, and rinse the filter before storing it.

finalTake: The AIPER Scuba V3 is the right robot pool cleaner for most in-ground pools because it plans its path and cleans from floor to waterline without a cord. Pick the Scuba S1 for irregular pools, the Dolphin CC Plus for 40 foot pools, and a Y20 for flat above-ground ones. Measure the pool first.
